article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: 2 Scoops × Lemon Tree
Breeder: Elev8 Seeds
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Lemon zest, citrus candy, orange sherbet
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Lemon Sherbet takes two very different interpretations of citrus cannabis and forces them into the same flower. One parent supplies creamy orange, grape sweetness, frost, and an almost frozen-dessert richness; the other brings a sharp lemon aroma intense enough to dominate a room. The result is weed with considerably more dimension than a simple lemon strain.

Fresh citrus peel, sour lemon candy, orange cream, sweet fruit, and a faint funky edge can appear in successive layers, while resinous flowers carry a potent hybrid experience that starts with brighter mental energy before gradually becoming more physically settled. Where many dessert cultivars place sweetness above everything else, this hybrid keeps enough Sour Diesel and Lemon Skunk character in the background to prevent the Sherbet side from becoming overly soft or sugary.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-verified formula is 2 Scoops × Lemon Tree, with 2 Scoops itself consisting of Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet . Elev8 obtained its 2 Scoops selection from T-Fly Genetics and has repeatedly emphasized that parent’s unusually strong orange push-pop aroma, heavy frost, and loud terpene expression. The combination of grape and orange Sherbet genetics provides the creamy, sweet side of Lemon Sherbet’s personality while contributing the dense resin coverage that made 2 Scoops useful throughout Elev8’s breeding catalog.

Lemon Tree pushes the cross in a dramatically sharper direction. Elev8 identifies its Lemon Tree cut as an elite Southern California selection descended from Lemon Skunk × Sour Diesel and describes it as an especially lemon-dominant phenotype. The Sour Diesel influence introduces a sour, funky depth behind the citrus, while Lemon Skunk reinforces brightness and pungency. Elev8 currently continues working extensively with Lemon Tree, describing the plant as resin-rich, high yielding, and relatively moderate in stretch.

The finished family tree therefore contains several distinct flavor traditions: Grape Sherbet, Orange Sherbet, Lemon Skunk, and Sour Diesel. That combination explains why the cultivar can move between sweet, creamy fruit and piercing citrus without settling entirely into either category. It also separates Lemon Sherbet from unrelated marijuana strains that share the same or a similar name. For the Elev8 Seeds version, 2 Scoops × Lemon Tree is the documented lineage.
Effects and Experience

The psychoactive experience generally makes sense when viewed through the Lemon Tree side first. A moderate amount can produce a relatively quick mental shift, with mood becoming brighter and sensory details more engaging. Music may feel sharper, conversation easier to follow, and creative or recreational activities more compelling. Lemon Tree itself is associated by Elev8 with an energizing cerebral opening followed by smoother physical relaxation, a progression that provides useful context for the experience inherited by its offspring.

As the session develops, the Sherbet side becomes easier to recognize. The body may begin to feel calmer while the faster mental component gradually rounds out, creating a hybrid state rather than an exclusively stimulating high. Instead of the immediate couch-lock associated with many heavy indica cultivars, relaxation tends to build beneath the initial uplift. Moderate servings may therefore fit socializing, listening to music, gaming, creative projects, or an easy evening, while heavier consumption is more likely to reduce motivation and produce stronger physical heaviness.

Elev8 does not publish a standardized THC percentage for the original Lemon Sherbet release, so assigning one universal potency number would be misleading. THC levels can vary with phenotype, environment, harvest maturity, and testing method. THC can also affect memory, emotions, judgment, coordination, and time perception; larger amounts may trigger anxiety, fear, paranoia, or panic in susceptible consumers. Batch-specific laboratory results are therefore more informative than a generic number attached to the strain name.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mental uplift and later physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers seeking cannabis that does not begin with immediate sedation. Some people gravitate toward balanced THC-rich hybrids when discomfort, tension, appetite changes, or difficulty relaxing interferes with normal activities. Lemon Sherbet’s bright opening may also be preferable to heavier weed for consumers who want to remain socially or mentally engaged before the more relaxing phase develops.

Those possibilities should not be presented as proven effects of this individual cultivar. No controlled clinical research establishes Lemon Sherbet as a treatment for chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical disorder. Broader research on cannabis and cannabinoids has found modest evidence of benefit for some forms of chronic pain, although the average improvement may be small and adverse effects occur more often with cannabinoid treatment than placebo in some studies. Certain cannabinoid medications also have recognized uses for chemotherapy-related nausea and specific appetite-loss conditions.

High-THC cannabis can create medical tradeoffs as well. A dose that feels relaxing to one person may produce dizziness, cognitive impairment, sleepiness, or anxiety in another. Anyone considering marijuana for persistent pain, sleep difficulties, appetite problems, or another diagnosed health condition should take cannabinoid concentration, medication interactions, personal tolerance, and guidance from an appropriate healthcare professional into account.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Few elements of Lemon Sherbet are as straightforward as the first smell: lemon arrives immediately. Elev8 selected Lemon Tree specifically because of its exceptionally forceful citrus expression, describing the cut as far more intensely lemon-forward than strains carrying only a faint citrus accent. In this hybrid, that character meets the sweeter 2 Scoops profile, which the breeder compares with old-school orange push-pop candy mixed with noticeable funk.

The combined aroma can resemble lemon zest scattered over orange sherbet. Sharp citrus oil leads, followed by orange cream, sweet fruit, sour candy, and a deeper funky element. Some phenotypes may emphasize the cleaner lemon side, while others lean more strongly toward creamy Sherbet sweetness. Grape can appear quietly underneath the brighter citrus tones, particularly in plants expressing more of the 2 Scoops parent.

Flavor follows the same layered pattern. Lemon and sour citrus dominate the initial inhale before creamier orange and sweet fruit become more apparent. The finish can reveal earth, mild fuel, and fermented funk from the Lemon Tree ancestry, keeping the palate from becoming one-dimensional. Elev8 has not published a standardized laboratory terpene panel for Lemon Sherbet, so exact dominant terpenes should be determined from testing of the individual harvest rather than inferred solely from aroma.
Growing Information

Elev8 Seeds lists an indoor flowering window of approximately eight to nine weeks, with its detailed product data also identifying an eight-week flowering time for some plants. That places the cultivar in a manageable middle range for photoperiod cannabis: considerably quicker than long tropical sativas, but with enough flowering time to develop dense resin and a mature citrus-dessert aroma.

Its parents offer useful clues about plant behavior. 2 Scoops flowers in approximately nine weeks and was selected for good production, substantial trichome coverage, and particularly intense terpenes. Lemon Tree finishes somewhat faster at roughly seven to eight weeks, while Elev8 describes its modern Lemon Tree line as high yielding, resin-rich, and relatively restrained in stretch. Lemon Sherbet offspring can therefore reasonably vary between more compact Lemon Tree-influenced expressions and somewhat fuller Sherbet-oriented plants.

An intermediate grow difficulty is appropriate because phenotype selection matters. Early topping or gentle low-stress training can help create an even canopy, while adequate airflow becomes important as resinous flowers gain density during the latter portion of bloom. Elev8 does not publish standardized indoor or outdoor yield figures or an official outdoor harvest date for Lemon Sherbet itself. Growers should therefore avoid treating secondary yield estimates as breeder specifications and determine maturity from flower development and trichome condition rather than a fixed calendar date.
FAQ
Is Lemon Sherbet indica or sativa?

Elev8 Seeds officially classifies Lemon Sherbet simply as a hybrid rather than assigning a precise indica/sativa percentage. Its experience can combine an uplifting cerebral beginning with gradually stronger physical relaxation.
What are the genetics of Lemon Sherbet?
The verified genetics are 2 Scoops (Grape Sherbet × Orange Sherbet) × Lemon Tree. Elev8’s Lemon Tree descends from Lemon Skunk × Sour Diesel.
Who bred Lemon Sherbet?
The version covered here was released by Elev8 Seeds using its selected 2 Scoops and Lemon Tree genetics. Elev8 now lists the strain as retired.
What does Lemon Sherbet taste like?

Expect sharp lemon zest, sour citrus, orange sherbet, creamy sweetness, fruit, and mild funk. The 2 Scoops parent contributes orange-dessert qualities, while Lemon Tree supplies the much louder lemon component.
How long does Lemon Sherbet take to flower?
Elev8 lists approximately eight to nine weeks, with eight weeks appearing in the breeder’s detailed strain specifications. Individual plants may finish at slightly different points within that range.
Final Thoughts on Lemon Sherbet

Lemon Sherbet works because its parents approach sweetness from opposite directions. 2 Scoops brings Grape Sherbet, Orange Sherbet, frost, creamy citrus, and candy-like richness; Lemon Tree introduces Lemon Skunk × Sour Diesel genetics with a much sharper lemon character and sour-funky edge. Instead of disappearing into generalized dessert sweetness, the citrus remains bright enough to define the finished flower.

That balance also extends to the experience and cultivation . An eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle keeps the plant practical, while the high can move from brighter cerebral engagement toward increasingly comfortable physical relaxation. For consumers who enjoy citrus marijuana but want more depth than a straightforward Lemon Skunk-style profile, the combination of lemon peel, orange sherbet, cream, fruit, and funk gives this retired Elev8 cultivar a clear identity. In a cannabis market filled with sweet weed, Lemon Sherbet stands apart by making genuine citrus intensity—not sugar alone—the centerpiece.
